placements.title: Nothing deploys without a signed release manifest
placements.frame: What must a release carry before it ships, where does that requirement bind, who owns it, and what prompted it?
placements.why: The CTO's rule (src-1), the incident behind it (src-2), and the memo's gate, scope and owner lines (src-3 to src-5) all describe one deployment gate. Future envelopes on release integrity, signing, and gate ownership will keep feeding this theme, so it is a subject rather than a one-off fact. The two unsigned artifacts are evidence for the theme and sit in the position, not in a leaf of their own.

mints.name: MeridianDeployGate
mints.title: Signed release manifests, gate scope, and ownership for Meridian deployments
mints.why: The org's own terms 'gate' and 'signed release manifest' name what the members are about together. Later documents on release gating will join this grouping.

mints.name: ReleaseQualityGates
mints.title: Quality review gates and change management
mints.why: A deployment sign-off requirement is a quality-review and change-management gate in the Organization/Process domain.

connections.why: The leaf is about the deployment gate itself and does the work of a process gate.
The position holds the gate requirement, its scope, its owner, and the incident that prompted it.
